rows.notes: The study is a desk-based review of the CSR reports and public communications of five coffee companies (Tim Horton's, Dunkin' Donuts, Tchibo, Starbucks, Nestl<U+00E9>), combined with a literature review on climate adaptation and CSR theory. It reports no own field data, experiment, survey or model runs; its 'results' are a qualitative document analysis of corporate reports, which is a review/opinion-type synthesis, so Q1 is 'no'. Irrigation of any kind (drip or sensor-based) is never mentioned; the only water-related text is a generic recommendation that 'improved soil and water management' and 'improving water collection and management' could be adaptation actions, attributed to other sources (Cohn et al. 2017; Davis et al. 2012; Laderach et al. 2017). The study provides no evidence on drip or sensor-based irrigation for drought resilience in coffee or Southeast Asia.

notes: Full text appears complete (pages 1-13). The study is a CSR/policy analysis of coffee companies' adaptation strategies, not a primary study of irrigation technology; the citation for drip/sensor-based irrigation in Southeast Asia is not supported by any content in this document.
